screenSizeIn.label: screen size
screenSizeIn.contradictionsObserved: 6 of 53 give two sizes. Real examples: 3KRsP5G (selected variant 83", key feature 65"), UXXAg59 (title '65 inch', key feature 'Screen Size Class: 55 Inch', store width 48.2 in in all three offers, which is a 55-inch TV), BNmn7U3 (key feature 55", description 65-inch).
screenSizeIn.normalization: Accept N", N”, N inch, N-inch, N-in, N" class, N cm (divide by 2.54). Ignore numbers followed by W, H or D (cabinet dimensions) and ranges such as 'fits 43 to 98 inch TVs' (mount bundles).

panelFamily.label: screen type

vesaPattern.label: wall-mount pattern

requirements.name: Fits the wall mount the buyer already has
requirements.whenStatedValue: If the request gives the mount's pattern or its maximum ('our mount takes up to 200 x 200'), it is a stated requirement: a listing whose pattern does not fit is broken and goes back to the agent without a question.

line.never_asked: This TV uses the VESA {vesaPattern} wall-mount pattern (the hole spacing on its back). Does your mount support it?
line.unbacked: The listing does not give the wall-mount pattern (VESA). Is that OK?
line.contradictory: The listing gives two wall-mount patterns: {conflicts}. Is that OK?

requirements.name: Fits the spot it goes in
requirements.whenStatedValue: If the request gives the available width ('the cabinet opening is 50 inches'), it is a stated requirement: a wider TV is broken and goes back to the agent without a question.

line.never_asked: This TV is {widthIn} inches wide. Is there room for that in the spot it goes?
line.unbacked: The store does not give this TV's width. Is that OK?
line.contradictory: The stores give different widths for this TV: {conflicts}. Is that OK?

outOfScope.name: Dolby Vision, HDR10+, HDR formats
outOfScope.reason: Removed on 2026-11-10 (Walter). Quality preferences: non-Dolby Vision TVs still play iPhone HDR video as HLG; HDR10+ and Dolby Vision streaming fall back to HDR10. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/av-foundation/Incorporating-HDR-video-with-Dolby-Vision-into-your-apps.pdf and https://engineering.fb.com/2025/11/17/ios/enhancing-hdr-on-instagram-for-ios-with-dolby-vision/

outOfScope.name: 120 Hz for game consoles
outOfScope.reason: Removed on 2026-11-10 (Walter). PS5 and Xbox Series X run at 60 Hz on a 60 Hz TV; 120 Hz is a preference.
